subject: Clarify treatment of transactions that span SOC 2 period end — evidence & bridge letter request
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@cg-audit.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: audit-team@cloudgrid.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify how to count transactions that begin before/finish after the SOC 2 window

Hi Grace,

Quick question from the audit team as we're preparing the Type II testing plan for CloudGrid's Redwood integration. For operational controls that produce time-ordered events (e.g., ingest transactions, long-running transform jobs), do you want us to consider the completion timestamp only, or should we count events whose start time is inside the window even if they complete after the period end?

For example: a job submitted 2027-05-31T23:50:00Z and completed 2027-06-01T00:05:00Z — the start is inside May window but completion is in June. Which moment aligns with your control descriptions for the audit?

Also, to finalize our evidence request we need a short manifest mapping event sources (API logs, worker traces, retention config) to the timestamps you consider authoritative. Can you confirm who on your side should provide that manifest and whether Redwood can provide a short bridge-letter style statement that we can include in the report to explain how you treat in-flight transactions at period boundaries?

If useful, I've attached a short sample-bridge-letter-template and a CSV example for the manifest we typically request.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Chen
Senior Auditor — CG Audit Partners

Attachment(s): sample-bridge-letter-template.docx, requested-log-manifest-sample.csv

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@cg-audit.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify how to count transactions that begin before/finish after the SOC 2 window

Thanks Laura — tagging Karthik (controls lead) to confirm our internal standard but wanted to capture our current thinking and ask for any auditor-preferred language for the bridge letter.

Short answers:
- Our operational control descriptions generally reference the completion/terminal timestamp for the action (i.e., when the persistent state change or audit log entry is recorded).
- Exceptions exist for controls that are explicitly start-triggered (e.g., job acceptance acknowledgements) — those are described in the control narratives.

What we can provide now:
1) A manifest mapping log sources and the canonical timestamp field we consider authoritative (API request.received_at, worker.job.completed_at, DB transaction.commit_ts).
2) A short bridge-letter draft confirming Redwood's interpretation: that the forensic evidence for this assertion is keyed to the completion timestamp unless otherwise stated in the control.

Open items for Karthik and infra:
- Confirm retention windows for ephemeral worker traces (we retain detailed worker traces for 45 days; aggregated metrics for 365 days).
- Export a small sample (10–20 rows) of completion timestamps across April–June to demonstrate the extraction process.

Laura — would the auditor prefer a narrow explicit wording ("completion timestamp governs inclusion in the audit period") or more conditional language that says "completion timestamp governs inclusion unless control narrative specifies start-based measurement"?

Grace O'Connor
Director, Trust & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): none

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@cg-audit.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 13:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify how to count transactions that begin before/finish after the SOC 2 window

Grace — thanks, that is helpful. For the report wording our preference is concise and unambiguous. Suggested phrasing: 

"Redwood Inference represents that, unless a control narrative explicitly identifies the initiating timestamp as the control objective, events will be included in the audit period based on the canonical completion/commit timestamp as recorded in Redwood's operational logs."

That language lets us be precise in the testing work and avoids back-and-forth during documentation review. If you can supply:
- The manifest CSV mapping source -> canonical_timestamp_field -> example_row_count
- A small sample extract (JSON or CSV) showing the canonical timestamps for cross-checking with the logs we pull
- A brief sentence in the bridge letter describing any controls that intentionally treat the start timestamp as authoritative

That should be sufficient for our Type II testing plan. I attached the template we typically use (sample-bridge-letter-template.docx) — feel free to edit directly.

One more note: please include retention/availability notes for ephemeral stores (e.g., KV cache) in the manifest so we can mark those as out-of-scope or in-scope for evidence collection.

Best,
Laura

Attachment(s): sample-bridge-letter-template.docx

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Action: prepare manifest + sample extract for CloudGrid audit (see thread)

Karthik — forwarding the auditor guidance below. Action items we need to close by EOD Mon 2027-06-07 so we can get the bridge letter back to the auditor:

1) Produce the manifest CSV mapping:
   - source (api_gateway, worker_service, db_commit_log)
   - canonical_timestamp_field (request.received_at, job.completed_at, transaction.commit_ts)
   - retention (days)
   - in-scope? (yes/no)

2) Export a 20-row sample extract containing the canonical timestamp fields across Apr–Jun 2027. Save as example-completion-timestamp-extract.json and upload to the shared drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-example-manifest
3) Review the suggested bridge letter language from the auditor (they prefer a completion-timestamp-first phrasing). If any control narratives truly require start-based inclusion, list them and provide one-sentence rationale.

I'll prepare a first-pass bridge letter using their template and drop it in the drive folder for your review. Please also confirm the retention note for ephemeral traces (we said 45 days earlier) and whether infra can produce the extract and manifest by the deadline.

Thanks — Grace

Grace O'Connor
Director, Trust & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): example-completion-timestamp-extract.json (to be uploaded)
